answer:
Yes. Multiple sources report that GLP-1 receptor agonists, especially semaglutide, reduce cardiovascular events. In a meta-analysis of 17 studies with over 40,000 patients, semaglutide significantly reduced cardiovascular death by 23%, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) by 18%, expanded MACE by 22%, nonfatal myocardial infarction by 18%, and nonfatal stroke by 32% [6]. Network meta-analyses also suggest semaglutide has the highest probability of cardiovascular benefit among GLP-1RAs and reduces MACE more than several other agents [1][2].

The benefits appear independent of weight loss, as earlier drug versions that produced little weight loss still cut MACE by about 20% [4]. Semaglutide also improved blood pressure, lipoproteins, and other risk factors, and in patients with chronic kidney disease, the FLOW trial showed an 18% MACE reduction [6]. Clinical guidelines now recommend considering GLP-1s as first-line treatment for weight management in obesity to reduce cardiovascular risk [4], and real-world evidence supports lower healthcare resource use with semaglutide in patients with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease [3]. Overall, the evidence clearly supports cardiovascular protection with semaglutide.
